city.Kosovo.description: Kosovo is one of Europe's youngest countries, tucked into the Balkans of southeastern Europe. It's known for its very young population, hillside medieval monasteries, and the dramatic cliffs and caves of Rugova Canyon.

city.Latvia.description: Latvia is one of three small Baltic countries in northern Europe, sitting between Estonia and Lithuania. Its capital, Riga, is famous for curly Art Nouveau buildings, and more than half the country is covered in green forest.
city.Latvia.landmark: red-brick towers of Turaida Castle rising above the autumn forest of the Gauja valley
city.Latvia.flag: dark reddish-brown with one white stripe across the middle

city.Liechtenstein.description: Liechtenstein is a tiny country high in the Alps, squeezed between Switzerland and Austria. It has no airport and no army, and a prince still rules from a castle perched above the capital, Vaduz.
city.Liechtenstein.landmark: Vaduz Castle perched on a wooded hillside above the town
city.Liechtenstein.greeting: People speak German here — say hello with “Grüezi” (GROO-tsee).
city.Liechtenstein.flag: blue on top, red on the bottom, with a little gold crown in the corner

city.Lithuania.description: Lithuania is the southernmost of the three Baltic countries in northern Europe. It's known for the astonishing Hill of Crosses, a red-brick castle on a lake island at Trakai, and golden amber washed up along its shore.
city.Lithuania.landmark: red-brick Trakai Island Castle on its lake
city.Lithuania.flag: yellow on top, green in the middle, red at the bottom
